name: Proton accelerator
line: Speeds protons up to the energy needed to make neutrons.

name: Proton source
line: Where the protons are produced before they enter the accelerator.

name: Radio-frequency supply
line: Supplies radio-frequency power to accelerate the protons.

name: Waveguide
line: Carries radio-frequency power from the supply to the accelerator.

name: Beam line
line: A vacuum pipe with magnets that steers the protons from the accelerator to the target.

name: Vacuum pump
line: Keeps the beam pipe empty of air so the protons travel freely.

name: Cooling manifold
line: Distributes cooling water to equipment during beam production.

name: Overhead crane
line: Lifts heavy equipment in and out for maintenance.

name: Area radiation monitor
line: Displays the radiation level for staff in the hall.

name: Hall access door
line: Provides access for staff and equipment maintenance.

name: Cable tray
line: Carries cables that supply power and signals to the equipment.

name: Target
line: The proton beam strikes the target here to produce the neutrons used for treatment.

name: Beam-shaping assembly
line: Slows fast neutrons from the target into a clinical epithermal beam: neutrons in the energy range used for treatment.

name: Treatment couch
line: Holds the patient in the planned position at the beam opening.

name: Beam-shaping assembly
line: Slows fast neutrons from the target into a clinical epithermal beam: neutrons in the energy range used for treatment.

name: Head mask
line: A moulded mask that keeps the head still during treatment.

name: Alignment lasers
line: Light lines used to set the patient in the planned position.

name: Observation camera
line: Lets staff watch the patient from the control room throughout treatment.

name: Intercom
line: Patient and staff can speak to each other during treatment.

name: Emergency stop
line: Lets staff stop the beam.

name: Positioning aid storage
line: Keeps positioning aids available when staff prepare the patient.

name: Shielding wall
line: Part of the room's radiation shielding.

name: Maze
line: The bent corridor into the treatment room; its turns are designed to reduce radiation reaching the door.

name: Shielded door
line: Closes the entrance to the treatment area during irradiation, when the beam is on.

name: Area radiation monitor
line: Displays the radiation level for staff near the treatment entrance.

name: Emergency stop
line: Lets staff stop the beam.

name: Control desk
line: Staff start, watch and stop the treatment from here.

name: Treatment status display
line: Lets staff follow the progress of treatment.

name: Patient observation display
line: Lets staff watch the patient during treatment.

name: Safety interlock panel
line: Designed so that the beam can run only when the room is clear and the door is closed.

name: Interlock status indicator
line: Tells staff whether the safety interlock conditions, the checks needed before the beam can run, are satisfied.

name: Infusion chair
line: The patient receives the boron drug here before treatment.

name: Infusion bag
line: Holds fluid for delivery to the patient during preparation.

name: Infusion stand
line: Holds the infusion bag beside the patient.

name: Nursing preparation counter
line: Gives staff a work surface for preparing patient care.

name: Privacy curtain
line: Gives the patient privacy during preparation.

name: Treatment planning workstation
line: Staff plan the dose to the tumour from the patient's images.

name: Positioning couch
line: Supports the patient while staff prepare the treatment position.

name: Mask storage
line: Keeps patient positioning masks ready for use.

name: Reception counter
line: Patients and visitors speak with reception staff here.

name: Waiting chair
line: Gives patients and visitors a place to rest before their appointment.

name: Main entrance doors
line: Connect the arrival area to reception.

name: Entrance canopy
line: Shelters patients and visitors as they approach the entrance.

name: Entrance path
line: Connects the arrival area to the patient entrance.

name: Drop-off area
line: Lets patients leave their vehicle close to the entrance.

name: Recovery chair
line: The patient rests here and is observed after treatment.

name: Handwashing basin
line: Lets patients wash their hands near the recovery space.

name: CT scanner
line: Images the patient so the treatment can be planned.

name: Boron measurement bench
line: Staff measure how much boron is in the patient's blood before treatment.

name: Water phantom
line: A water tank used to measure the beam and check it before patients are treated.

name: Beam generation
line: Houses the accelerator and the proton beam line.

name: Treatment room
line: The patient receives the neutron beam here.

name: Control room
line: Staff supervise treatment from outside the treatment room.

name: Reception
line: Patients and visitors arrive and ask for assistance here.

name: Recovery
line: Patients rest under observation after treatment.

name: Imaging
line: Patient images support treatment planning.

name: Boron laboratory
line: Measures how much boron is in the patient's blood.

name: Quality-assurance laboratory
line: Staff check the beam here before patients are treated.

name: Consultation
line: Patients discuss their care with clinical staff.

name: Follow-up
line: Staff review patient progress after treatment.

name: Cooling plant
line: Cooling equipment removes heat from treatment equipment.

name: Electrical plant
line: Electrical equipment supplies the facility systems.

name: Maintenance
line: Staff service equipment here.

name: Infusion
line: Patients receive the boron drug before treatment.

name: Treatment planning
line: Staff prepare the treatment plan using patient images.

name: Positioning
line: Staff prepare the patient position before treatment.

name: Maze access
line: The turning entrance leads to the treatment room.

name: Staff room
line: Staff take breaks away from patient care spaces.

name: Staff offices
line: Staff coordinate patient care and facility work here.

name: Washroom
line: Provides a nearby toilet and handwashing space for patients.
